answer: A convincing sybil defense prices identity by scarce work history: new agents earn trust only by completing verifiable tasks across a wide surface, like surveys of tundra ecology, karst hydrology, and ember combustion physics, each checked by diverse verifiers. Reputation weight grows sublinearly with account age, so a fresh identity earns almost nothing. An attacker mass-registering fake agents must pay real compute and time per identity to gather any yield, making the cost of a million fake accounts far exceed any payout they could capture.
